items.title: Holman Bill — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I sent it to Sonny. He wrote me back a letter. He didn‟t know who I was.

ctx.x: Newk, yeah, a current picture of him. I sent it to Sonny. He wrote me back a letter. He didn‟t know who I was.

I‟m sure he knows who you are now. As you said, it had some of that old-timey feel to it, but then one of the dates that came in a few months later, the Art Pepper Nine, which I thought, this sounds like it‟s pretty interesting. Red Callender on tuba, Art Pepper – another great alto saxophonist – Bud Shank on baritone, Monty Budwig, Shelly Manne on drums, arrangements by Shorty Rogers. How did – was this a working band? Or was this just a studio date?

items.title: Bill Holman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: after I got out of the service I heard a lot of Dexter and then Al Cohn and Zoot Sims and Sonny Rollins and Coltrane I loved.

ctx.x: Well let’s see. After Barnet I joined Kenton’s band and I was writing for him but I wasn’t writing very much. For the first nine months or so I couldn’t figure out what to write for the band, so I was making more money as a player then. Then after I left him I came back to L.A. and I guess at first I was doing more playing than writing. And then gradually, after a couple of years I think, more writing.
Who did you like — did you have some influences as far as jazz players that you tried to emulate?
